text:
maya: heads up — I spotted duplicated billing tied to stream resume + route flip. Two charges for the same sequence after reconnect.

maya: logs snippet: 
```
[edge] time=2026-03-19T15:12:03Z tenant=tenant-45 resume_token=rb.resume.v1.eyJ... route=us-west-2->us-east-1 session=ss-9a7
request_id=rc-001 tokens_charged=120
...
[edge] time=2026-03-19T15:12:04Z tenant=tenant-45 resume_token=rb.resume.v1.eyJ... route=us-east-1 session=ss-9b0 request_id=rc-002 tokens_charged=120
```

adrian: :eyes: is this the mid-deploy route flip we talked about? sounds like resume went to a different shard so billing saw a new session.

maya: repro steps I used: open streaming SSE, send ~100 tokens, drop network mid-chunk, reconnect with same resume token, router picks different pool during canary swap. billing shows two charges. seen in prod pre-fix canary.

sam: what's our current dedupe key in metering? are we deduping on request_id or session_id?

paula: billing pipeline uses (session_id, sequence_range). resume generates a new session_id when routed to a new pool, so dedupe misses it.

adrian: that matches our earlier model: sticky-lease keeps session_id stable, but when route flips we create a new session. resume token isn't propagated to billing until later in pipeline.

maya: raw headers on reconnect: 
```
GET /v1/stream
Host: api.redwood.ai
x-resume-token: rb.resume.v1.eyJtenant:45...sig
x-client-session: ss-9a7
```

sam: can we use resume_token as the canonical dedupe key? if it's signed per-tenant it should be safe.

paula: concern: replay/abuse if resume_token can be reused by attacker. Need binding: resume_token must be tenant-scoped and include nonce/timestamp. If signed we can trust it for dedupe within a small window.

maya: the token looks signed (jwt-ish base64). example value in logs: `rb.resume.v1.eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...`

adrian: approach suggestion: 1) short-term: router should prefer sticky-lease for requests with x-resume-token for 5-10s to avoid split routing. 2) medium-term: add resume_token_hmac as a field into metering events so billing can dedupe by resume_token within grace_window. 3) long-term: update console and billing UX to show resumed dedupe status.

console-team: UX ask: we need a console filter/flag for "resumed streams that caused duplicate charges" and a way to surface refunds. Also add a dedupe tag on billing rows so SREs can triage.

infra-bot: deploy/checker: sticky-lease-affinity v1.2 rolled to canary at 2026-03-19T15:25:10Z (canary pool: us-east-1-a).

maya: after the canary rollout we still see a few dupes (small %), likely race where routing decision happened before lease-affinity update propagated.

sam: tests needed: e2e where router flips shard mid-resume and assert single billing event. Add a chaos test that terminates connection during reconnect window.

paula: operational mitigation: billing team will scan for duplicates where resume_token matches and time delta < 30s and issue refunds. I'll coordinate.

adrian: RFC/PR plan: I'll write an RFC to propagate resume_token into the metering event envelope and adjust dedupe logic. Short-term change to router is smaller and can be hot-fixed.

maya: lightweight server-side guard idea: if we receive a charge for a sequence range and there's a recent charge for same resume_token within last 10s, ignore second charge and emit metric `stream.resume_dedupe_skipped`.

console-team: add that metric to dashboards (per-tenant time series) and show a count on the stream trace view.

infra-bot: incident created INC-2026-0319-01 by maya.

paula: I'll open billing ticket and prepare refund script for obvious duplicates.

maya: attaching full logs and a small repro harness to the incident.

adrian: I'll start the RFC this afternoon and link to the incident. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
